newsitem.title: NORWAY: FORECAST - Storebrand 9-mo profits seen down.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Storebrand 9-mo profits seen down.

text.p: Norway's largest insurance company Storebrand ASA, facing increasing competition, is expected to post a slightly weaker group profit of 1.13 billion crowns for January-September, down from 1.28 billion crowns a year ago, according to seven analysts polled by Reuters.
One analyst had a buy recommendation on the share, three said hold and three said sell.
The Storebrand shares have gained close to 20 percent since the beginning of August and some analysts believe their short-term potential has now largely been exhausted.

Storebrand has said competition in the Norwegian insurance industry calls for better cost effectiveness throughout the group. The effect on the accounts of the planned restructuring measures -- a provision of possibly between 150 and 300 million crowns -- will be recorded in the third quarter of this year.
Analysts did not incorporate these costs in the forecast for the nine-month results, but they were included in Earnings Per Share projections for 1996 and onwards.
The company will present the results on November 6.
NOTE -- The company on October 1 shortened its name to Storebrand ASA, dropping the word "UNI" as part of a campaign to streamline its image.
